items.title: Human-headed winged lion (lamassu)
items.alt_neutral: Colossal grey stone gateway figure: a bearded human head in a tall horned cap on a lion's body with wings and five legs; feathered wings fill the slab and lines of incised text run between the legs

made.note: Carved for a palace gateway at Nimrud

journey_fact.text: Excavated at Nimrud under A. H. Layard in the 1840s (export not documented); given in 1849 to Lady Charlotte Guest, Canford Manor, England; sold to D. Kelekian 1919, J. D. Rockefeller 1927; given to the Met 1930 (accessioned 1932).

facts.text: The sculptor gave it five legs, so it looks firmly planted when seen from the front and striding forward when seen from the side.
Ashurnasirpal II made Nimrud his capital and in 879 BCE feasted 69,574 people for ten days to celebrate it.
